newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli settler charged in Arab boy's death.
newsitem.headline: Israeli settler charged in Arab boy's death.

text.p: Israeli authorities on Friday charged the security chief of a Jewish settlement with the killing of an 11-year-old Palestinian boy, saying he beat the child on the head with a pistol butt after chasing suspected stone-throwers.
Hilmi Shousha, from the village of Husan in the West Bank, died in an Israeli hospital on Monday of a brain haemorrhage, a day after Arab witnesses said Nahum Kurman had beaten him.
Kurman faces up to 20 years in jail if convicted of the manslaughter charge, spelled out in gruesome detail in an indictment sheet distributed to reporters.
It was not immediately clear if Kurman, who denied at a previous remand hearing that he had killed the boy, was asked to enter a plea.

"The accused, security chief of Hadar Beitar (settlement), entered Husan village in a jeep while carrying a pistol with the aim of detaining youths who, according to reports he received earlier, had stoned a car," the indictment said.

"As he was driving in the village, he chased (Hilmi and two cousins). After a 30-metre (yard) chase, he stopped the jeep, got down with a pistol in his hand and ran towards the deceased who stood near one of the houses.

"While standing face-to-face with the deceased, he hit him and kicked him in the head. As a result of the kick, the deceased fell and while he was lying on his back, the accused put his foot on his neck and hit him in the head with a pistol butt," the charge sheet said.
The blows to Hilmi's head tore the spinal artery, causing internal bleeding that led to his death, it said.

"Not only didn't I kill the boy but I did the utmost to save his life. I tried to resuscitate him and called an ambulance. I feel humilated. My greatest pain, of course is that the boy died," Kurman was quoted as saying in an interview with the Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper on Friday.
As he entered the court, Kurman, a religious Jew, kissed members of his family but said nothing to reporters.
Prosecutors said they planned to call 23 witnesses in the case.
Israeli troops clashed briefly with Husan residents on Tuesday after the boy's funeral.
In a rare gesture by a U.S. government official, Edward Abington, U.S. Consul-General in Jerusalem, paid a condolence call on Wednesday to the Shousha family in their West Bank home.
